summary: Revise at 5.8 (Caiman 7, ship 7.5). The rethink was the right call: a long ribbed trumpet with a five-pointed, recurved mouth next to a spined capsule is the thorn-apple pairing, and from the face it reads as datura without a caption. It is far from a master ring, though. (1) The theme stops at the badge. The palm and both lower shanks are the bare factory stock, polished smooth, and the 'polished stem' in the brief was never built, so the theme does not run from face to palm. (2) The leaves are the weakest passage. Their outlines are ragged and combed (face-zoom, stones.png), their veins are chevrons that read as tyre tread or oak-bark scales rather than datura venation, and their margins are angular plates rather than sinuate lobes. (3) The badge is about 40% bare flat plate (lower centre and lower right), and four clawed seeds in a diagonal stagger on that plate read as a pave line, not seeds spilling from a pod. (4) The trumpet projects about 10 mm past the badge edge into free air on the 205 deg bearing. It is a beautiful silhouette but a snag hazard, and Logan should see the wearability trade. (5) Seen from the side, the capsule is a smooth upright cylinder with sparse cone studs and a lobed cap, which reads as a spiked mace or a helmeted head more than an egg-shaped burr. Gates: the geometry, castability, DFM, stones, reload and export gates are green and verified in report.json. The template gate has been run and FAILED: template_bytes 4,053,828 against a 1,000,000 stock budget, over the 3 MB flag, template_gate_passed false. verification.json is also stale: it was written at 18:09, but design.ring.json was rewritten at 19:02. That is an automatic revise on its own.
strengths: The trumpet flower is the best form on the ring: a long, swelling ribbed tube, a five-pointed corolla with recurved hooked tips, a clean silhouette against black in hero, side and shoulder. It names the plant.
Flower plus spined capsule is the correct datura pairing, and the face-300 reads as datura to a plant-literate eye, as read-test 5 found.
The seeds are in made settings (seat bur plus three-claw heads, the claws curled like small thorns), coloured black as datura seeds are, and two are now visible inside the split capsule.
The silhouette is unlike any other Vepres ring: an asymmetric horn breaking out of a signet. No other ring in the collection has a single object leaving the outline like this.
The factory 011 Badge keeps its hard wall-to-face angles and sinuate calyx outline (bare-vs-finished).

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: The theme is confined to the badge table. In palm.png and reverse.png the shank, shoulders below the table and palm are bare polished stock, with no stem, no leaf and no tendril. The 'polished stem' palm in the brief was not built. The lower right leaf (leaf 4/5, bearing 295-345) is an isolated fragment.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: In face-300 the trumpet with a pointed five-tipped mouth beside a spined ball reads as datura or thorn-apple. It reads narrowly: in hero-300 the capsule seen side-on is a studded cylinder, and the leaves read as feathers or oak leaves.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: Leaves 1-3 (bearing 140-198) show ragged combed edges and torn vein grooves in face-zoom.png and stones.png. Their 'serrations' are faceted stair-step plates. The capsule valve lips also show a frayed rim at the split (stones.png, top centre). The flower and spines are clean.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as fruit or buds
checklist.reason: 8 black spinel 1.5 in seat bur plus three-claw thorn heads; black matches datura seed. Weaknesses: the four spilled seeds sit in a near-straight diagonal on bare plate, and pod seeds 1-4 are crowded at 0.56-0.63 mm (reported, not gating). Only 2 of the 4 pod seeds show in face-zoom.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The capsule body is a smooth cylinder with evenly spaced cone studs, which is mechanical. The leaves are angular faceted plates. The bare table plate is flat and blocky. The flower is properly sculpted.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The 011 Badge wall-to-table edge and sinuate outline are intact in bare-vs-finished.png and hero.png.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: The horn breaking from a signet is unique in the collection. Its wearability needs Logan's eye (see the punch list).

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: There are large forms (flower, capsule) and small ones (spines, seeds), but the medium tier (leaves) is weak, and about 40% of the table plus the entire shank and palm are empty. That is well below the Caiman hero's all-over density.

gates.gate: Template gate: <= 4 design.set patches within class budget
gates.claimed: report gates_passed true (the template gate is not counted there)
gates.verified: verification.json: 1 design.set patch (/manufacturing) is fine, but template_bytes 4,053,828 against a size_budget_bytes of 1,000,000 for the stock class, size_review_required true, template_gate_passed false. It is over the 3 MB flag.

punch_list.change: Bring the stock template under 1 MB. The stored meshes (capsule 390k triangles before cleaning, flower 72.8k, leaves 17.8k each) are being lifted as baked mesh. Rebuild the capsule as Revolve plus About spine patterns and the leaves as stamps or lofts, as the build plan specifies, so the template carries parameters, not triangles. Then rerun --verify against the current design.
punch_list.acceptance: A fresh verification.json, newer than design.ring.json, shows template_gate_passed true, template_bytes <= 1,000,000, design_set_patches <= 4 and vertices_faces_normals_identical true.

punch_list.zone: shank, palm and lower shoulders, theta 200-340 deg (all of it below the table)
punch_list.change: Carry the plant to the palm. Run the flower's stem as a raised, swept cane, 2.0-2.5 mm wide and 0.8-1.0 mm proud, from the trumpet's base under the table down one shoulder and round the palm, ending in a node. Add 2 small sinuate leaves (5-6 mm) and one tendril or bud on the opposite shoulder at about 300 deg, with a second spine-capsule bud of 3 mm if room allows.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png and reverse.png show a continuous raised stem on the shank, with no bare arc of more than 90 deg of shank. side.png shows plant form on both shoulders.

punch_list.zone: leaves 1-3 (bearings 140-198, upper-left table and the left shoulder) and leaves 4-5 (lower right)
punch_list.change: Rebuild every leaf with true outlines: a datura (Datura stramonium) sinuate outline with 3-4 broad, irregular, angular lobes per side, 1.0-1.5 mm deep, no stair-step facets. Use a raised midrib 0.4 mm wide with 3-4 paired side veins as smooth, rounded tier-1 ridges, not chevron grooves. Give the blades a gentle cupped or twisted curvature (0.5-1.0 mm of out-of-plane wave) so they are not flat plates.
punch_list.acceptance: In face-zoom.png and stones.png no leaf edge shows combing, fraying or stair-steps. The veins read as a midrib with paired laterals, not as a tread or herringbone. In face-300 the leaves read as lobed leaves, not feathers or oak leaves.

punch_list.zone: table plate: lower centre and lower right (below the capsule, right of the trumpet)
punch_list.change: Fill the bare plate. Bring leaf 4 up to about 9 mm and lay it across the lower right, lobing over the badge edge. Rearrange the 4 spilled seeds as a loose, curving fall out of the capsule's lowest split: spacing 1.5-2.5 mm, irregular, no three collinear, the last seed half under a leaf lobe. Optionally add a shallow chased seam of fallen-petal relief on the remaining plate.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png no flat bare region of the table is wider than about 4 mm. No three seeds are collinear within 0.3 mm. The seed fall visibly starts at the capsule's split.

punch_list.change: Make it an egg-shaped burr, not a studded cylinder. Swell the body to an ovoid (max diameter at about 40% of its height, 1.3:1). Raise the spine count on the flank to about 50, in 5 offset rows of varied length (1.0-1.8 mm), so the side-on outline is densely spined. Peel back 2 of the 4 valves 20-30 deg so the black seeds show from the hero camera. Clean the frayed valve-lip rim.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero-300 and side.png the capsule is an egg-shaped burr with spines breaking its outline on every side and no smooth cylindrical flank wider than 1.5 mm between spines. In hero.png at least 3 seeds are visible inside the split. stones.png shows a clean valve lip.

punch_list.zone: trumpet flower, bearing 205, free length past the badge
punch_list.change: Address wear. Either tuck the corolla down and back so it overhangs the badge edge by no more than 5 mm and sits within 4 mm of the shank's outer surface, curling round the shoulder, or keep the projection and report it to Logan as a deliberate statement piece with the overhang measured. Thicken the five recurved tip hooks to a section of at least 0.8 mm.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json records the flower's overhang past the table outline (mm) and its minimum tip section (>= 0.8 mm). The side.png silhouette still shows the open five-pointed mouth.
